findings.title: Seed-skip refusal deleted: a check-consistency round planting zero seeds now opens
locations: src/CLI/Rounds.jl:166-175 prepare (check-consistency) — refusal replaced by note_seed_skips!
src/CLI/Rounds.jl:273-278 seed_docs_corpus! (check-docs) — refusal replaced by note_seed_skips!; only the plan-empty refusal kept
src/CLI/Passes.jl:690-691 grade — the only reader of seed_skipped, a printed WARNING
test/seeds.jl:274-294 — tests note_seed_skips! directly, never prepare's outcome
findings.before:
if !isempty(skipped)
    println(io, "prepare: refused — $(length(skipped)) seed class(es) have no anchor in the manuscript: ", join(skipped, ", "))
    println(io, "         a skipped class is UNDEFINED in recall, so the denominator shrinks in silence;")
    ...
    return 2
end
findings.after:
note_seed_skips!(dir, rec, skipped, cfg["instruments"]["check-consistency"]["seed_catalog"]; io)
f2, s2 = Seeds.plant(f, s, plan)
write(full, f2); write(site, s2)
println(io, "prepare: $(length(plan)) seed(s) planted ...")
...
return 0
findings.why_it_matters: Input that was refused before: a seeded check-consistency round whose consolidated manuscript carries none of the catalogue's anchors. At base `skipped` was non-empty, so prepare returned 2. Now `Seeds.select` returns an empty plan, `Seeds.plant` does nothing and prepare prints "0 seed(s) planted" and exits 0. The round records `seed_salt`, bank writes a ground_truth.json with `seeded = []` (the schema has no minItems), and `Recall.per_class` reports every class UNDEFINED. The panel is paid for as a seeded round that measures nothing. check-docs still refuses exactly this case ("a round that plants nothing measures nothing"), so the two docs instruments now disagree. Where only some classes skip, the round closes and can be cited by a release like a full one: nothing at close, in release or in the tally reads `seed_skipped`. Recall over k of n classes is then compared with recall over n, and the only trace is a warning line at prepare and grade.
findings.description: The refusal went from both prepare paths. The stated reason, that refusing a partly plantable round trades a narrowed measurement for none, covers the partial case. It does not cover the check-consistency path, which lost its only guard against an empty plan: check-docs kept its plan-empty refusal and check-consistency never had one. Nothing downstream treats a narrowed measurement differently from a full one either, so the silence the refusal was added to end is now a printed line and a record field no gate reads.
findings.evidence: Rounds.jl:272-277 (check-docs keeps): `if isempty(plan) println(io, "prepare: refused — the seed catalogue matched nothing in the lane surfaces" ...) return 2`. The check-consistency path at Rounds.jl:166-175 has no such branch. Passes.jl:690: `sk = String.(get(rec, "seed_skipped", String[])); isempty(sk) || println(io, "grade: WARNING — ...")`, and no other reader exists (rg seed_skipped over src). ground-truth.schema.json `seeded`: `{"items": {...}, "type": "array"}`, no minItems.

findings.title: Claim checklist floor narrowed: 140 lines gone, the backticked exit contract among them
locations: test/rounds.jl:245-255 — the new assertions pin only the unbackticked exit form and the dropped cases
findings.before:
const CLAIM_EXIT = r"...|\bexit\s+contract\b[^.]{0,60}?[0-3]\b"i
const CLAIM_QUANTIFIER = r"\b(?:every|never|always|all|none|any|only)\b"i
const CLAIM_TOOL_ID = r"...|\bgbg\s+[a-z]+\b"
qu = occursin(CLAIM_QUANTIFIER, s) && occursin(CLAIM_TOOL_ID, s)
findings.after:
const CLAIM_EXIT = r"...|\bexit\s+contract\b[^.]{0,60}?(?<![\w.])[0-3]\s+[a-z]"i
const CLAIM_QUANTIFIER = r"\b(?:every|never|always|none)\b"i
const CLAIM_TOOL_ID = r"...|`gbg\s+[a-z]+"
const CLAIM_CLAUSE = r"(?<=[.;!?])\s+|\s+—\s+"
qu = any(c -> occursin(CLAIM_QUANTIFIER, c) && occursin(CLAIM_TOOL_ID, c), split(s, CLAIM_CLAUSE))
findings.why_it_matters: `claim_checklist` is documented as "the mechanical floor under one check-docs lane", and `checklist_files` refuses to truncate it because "a silently halved one would read as a complete list". I ran the base and head regexes over the tool's own surfaces (src, ext, docs/src/guide, ARCHITECTURE.md, policy, instruments, catalog, templates). The checklist falls from 809 lines to 669. The quantifier class alone falls from 442 to 201. 62 of the dropped lines still carry every, never, always or none together with a tool id; they fall out only because of the clause split, the unbackticked `gbg`, or a table cell's semicolon. Examples: `docs/src/guide/verbs.md:7` "The exit contract is one for all: `0`" (the backticked digit fails `[0-3]\s+[a-z]`); `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:1905` "`ROUND.OPEN` | lists open rounds (WARN; never FAIL"; `src/CLI/Gate.jl:33` "gate: ROUND.DIR — ... the gate never passes vacuously (gbg init writes it)". A seeded exit-code-drift or quantifier mutation planted on any of these lines is now off the checklist, so seeded recall across this change is not comparable.
findings.description: The defects cited were two false positives: the `1` of a version string, and a quantifier anywhere on a line that names any verb. The edit goes further than those need. It drops three quantifiers, requires backticks on `gbg`, scopes the match to a clause (splitting on every `. `, `;` and spaced dash, table cells included), and requires a lowercase word right after the exit digit, which the tool's own backticked guide prose never has. The new tests assert the dropped cases as intended ("`any` is ordinary prose") and check the exit contract only in an unbackticked form the corpus does not use. The oracle was written to fit the narrowed detector.
findings.evidence: Measured: `quantifier old=442 new=201`; `checklist lines old=809 new=669; dropped with a strong universal + tool id on the line = 62`; `exit ... dropped=1: docs/src/guide/verbs.md:7: ... The exit contract is one for all: \`0\``. Test at head: `@test occursin(P.CLAIM_EXIT, "the exit contract: 0 clean, 1 finding, 2 cannot evaluate")`, while verbs.md reads "The exit contract is one for all: `0`\nclean, `1` a substantive finding".

findings.title: gbg round build exits 0 when its ROUND.toml record fails to save
findings.before:
rec["build"] = Dict{String,Any}("code" => code, "head" => something(Git.head(cfg["root"]), "0"^40), "at" => timestamp())
save(dir, rec)
println(io, "build: exit $code — $log"); return code
findings.after:
try
    save(dir, rec)
catch err
    err isa RoundError || rethrow()
    had === nothing ? delete!(rec, "build") : (rec["build"] = had)
    return sprint(showerror, err)
end
...
println(io, "build: exit $code — $log", why === nothing ? " (recorded)" : "\nbuild: NOT RECORDED — $why; `close` will not see this build")
return code
findings.why_it_matters: `save` throws RoundError("ROUND.toml would not validate (a tool defect)"). At base that propagated to cmd_round's `err isa RoundError` arm, so `gbg round build` exited 2. Now, when the build is green and the record fails, the verb exits 0, although recording is its stated purpose. A session gating on exit codes ("a log is never grepped for a verdict") sees success, and learns otherwise only when close refuses. The same diff's ConfigWrittenError says the opposite: "a config this tool has just written failing to validate is a defect of the tool ... it must reach the crash path". A ROUND.toml the tool has just composed is the same case, and here it is swallowed to a printed line.
findings.description: The error is swallowed so that prepare and pass open can keep going after a build they now record. The swallowing also reached `gbg round build`, whose one extra duty is the record. The rollback of `rec["build"]` is correct, but the exit code no longer says whether that duty was done.
findings.evidence: Base cmd_round: `catch err; err isa RoundError || rethrow(); println(stderr, sprint(showerror, err)); return 2`. Rounds.jl:50 `isempty(errs) || throw(RoundError("ROUND.toml would not validate (a tool defect):\n  " ...))`. Rounds.jl:376 `return code`.

findings.title: gbg round scripts: unchecked precondition, and replacements that leave no record
locations: src/CLI/Preflight.jl:952 (a round opens with head "0"^40 when there is no HEAD)
findings.before:
statement = "An instrument is never changed mid-round; a change is its own commit and release; a deferral is written in the round's deferred.md and carried into the work queue at close."
...
dst = Preflight.copy_scripts(cfg, String(rec["instrument"]), round)
entry = Dict{String,Any}("at" => timestamp(), "head" => something(Git.head(cfg["root"]), "0"^40))
... save(dir, rec)
findings.after:
statement = "... a round whose own frozen scripts cannot run has the differing copies replaced by gbg round scripts --reason, recorded in ROUND.toml."
...
    Preflight.install_script(src, dst)
end
isempty(moved) && (println(io, "scripts: every frozen script of $round already equals the running copy's — nothing refreshed, nothing recorded"); return 0)
head = Git.head(cfg["root"])
head === nothing && throw(RoundError("scripts: the root has no git HEAD to record the refresh against"))
findings.why_it_matters: (1) The policy now permits a mid-round change only "for a round whose own frozen scripts cannot run". The code checks only a reason of at least 24 characters, so a round whose verifiers run fine can have a changed lens swapped in mid-round on any wording. The rule at base forbade that outright. (2) On a round opened without a git HEAD, which Preflight.jl:952 allows with its "0"^40 placeholder, the verb installs every differing script and then throws RoundError (exit 2) before writing `scripts_refreshed`. A re-run finds nothing different and prints "nothing refreshed, nothing recorded" with exit 0, so the replacement is permanent and unrecorded. At base the entry was always written, head "0"^40. (3) The no-op compares the frozen copy with the running copy, not with a sha taken at preflight, so a hand refresh (the unrecorded route this record exists to expose) now gets a clean exit 0 and no entry, where base's verb appended one.
findings.description: The frozen-mid-round rule was loosened in the policy text, with a condition that sounds narrow, while the code guard that went in (a reason length) does not test that condition. The reordering also lets an early throw leave scripts replaced with nothing recorded. The verb's record was the only visible trace of a mid-round script change, and in both paths that trace can now be missing.
findings.evidence: Rounds.jl:403 `length(strip(reason)) >= 24 || (... return 2)` is the only precondition. Rounds.jl:413 `Preflight.install_script(src, dst)` runs before Rounds.jl:417 `head === nothing && throw(RoundError(...))`. Preflight.jl:952 `head = something(Git.head(root), "0"^40)`.

findings.title: Step-0 import relaxations apply to every round and every directory
findings.why_it_matters: Three inputs that were refused are now accepted. (a) Any ROUND.toml, closed or open, with `config_sha = ""`. At base the schema made it :invalid, which the gate reports as a fatal exit 2. Now it validates, and on a closed round the blanked stamp goes unnoticed: ROUND.FROZEN's shas cover the evidence, not the stamps. (b) `gbg round import --empty <id> --reason "..."` run where no config is found. At base Config.read refused it with exit 2. Now the root falls back to the git top level, or failing that to pwd, so run from a non-consumer repository or a plain directory it writes `.gbg/rounds/<id>/` there and exits 0. `self_verify` returns 0 under a dev copy, and torn_check is skipped when there is no config. (c) `stamps(nothing)`, which was a MethodError, now silently yields an empty config stamp. The defect the change fixes is only the import's need to run before `init`. Nothing restricts the empty stamp to abandoned import records, or the no-config root to a package tree.
findings.description: The design wanted `import --empty` to run before `init`, and that part is justified. The relaxation, though, was made in shared contracts (the round schema and `stamps`) and in root resolution, with no scoping: the schema could have allowed `config_sha = ""` only with `abandoned` present, and the root could have required a Project.toml or a git repository. The test only covers the happy path in a bare temp directory.
findings.evidence: Diff: `-   "pattern": "^[0-9a-f]{64}$",` / `+   "pattern": "^([0-9a-f]{64}|)$",`. test/rounds.jl:960-965: `bare = mktempdir(); cd(bare) do ... @test G.main(["round", "import", "--empty", id, "--reason", why]) == 0` in a directory with no git repository and no Project.toml.

findings.title: close now accepts builds from prepare and pass open, including dirty-tree builds
findings.before:
# `build` records {code, head}; this reads it back.
if inst in Sync.DOCS_INSTRUMENTS
    b = get(rec, "build", nothing)
    if b === nothing
        push!(fails, "no docs build is recorded for this round — gbg round build $round")
findings.after:
`close`'s docs-build condition ... the round record carries a build (`Rounds.record_build!`, written by `prepare`, `pass open` and `gbg round build`)
...
# Reuse is refused on a dirty tree, where HEAD names nothing about what would be built.
...
code = Rounds.run_under_round(cfg, round, cfg["package"]["docs_build"]; log)
why = Rounds.record_build!(cfg, dir, rec, code)
findings.why_it_matters: Input refused before: `gbg round close` on a docs round where no `gbg round build` was ever run, for example one whose findings were all adjudicated. At base: "no docs build is recorded". Now the build from prepare or pass open satisfies it. pass open builds whatever the working tree holds and records it against HEAD, while the comment a few lines above says a dirty tree is one where HEAD names nothing about what would be built. close checks only the round directory for uncommitted files. So a green build of uncommitted edits under a covered path, later discarded without a commit, reads as current at close. The same hole existed at base through `gbg round build`; the diff adds two implicit entry points to it that run without the session asking for a build.
findings.description: Widening the verbs that satisfy close's build condition makes sense for a clean tree. But record_build! does not check porcelain, although pass_open's own reuse logic treats a dirty tree as having no meaningful HEAD.
findings.evidence: Passes.jl:555-559: `Reuse is refused on a dirty tree, where HEAD names nothing about what would be built ... reuse = k > 1 && isempty(Git.porcelain(root)) && ...`. Passes.jl:568 `why = Rounds.record_build!(cfg, dir, rec, code)` has no porcelain check. Passes.jl:1181 close: `dirty = [p for (_, p) in Git.porcelain(root) if startswith(p, rel * "/") || p == rel]` looks only at the round directory.
